verdict: Strong work that clears all sixteen acceptance criteria under execution — auditCatalog() returns [], the production.data.js diff is +132/-0 with no comment touched, the id is freightdepot and the collision with the existing 'depot' (Supply Workshop) is written down, CITY_PREREQ.freightdepot=['powerplant'] is one level deep and acyclic, depot.js exports exactly the eight pinned names, has zero bare globals, zero .from(/.rpc(, and every export returns a typed neutral from both the no-data path and the catch under nine driven failure shapes. The cost-dial comment's stated charge (35,000 cinder + 238 metal + 175 supplies + 125 stone + 75 fuel) matches buildingCostAt() exactly, and the sql/038 quotations (3 + depot_level at :795, least(2*depot_level, max_bays) at :999, greatest(1, least(3, ...)) at :1468) all check out. It falls just short of the bar on the one property this repo grades hardest: two of depot.js's most load-bearing cross-file claims are false when run, and depotReady() cannot enforce the rule its own comment states.
biggest_gap: depotReady()'s check-2 comment declares that 'telling a player to go and build a depot they may already own is the most expensive wrong sentence this screen can print', but the code only distinguishes a MISSING city module. When /src/city/index.js is registered while window.MythicCityBridge is absent or threw mid-construction, host() is null, MP.placed() returns [] and depotReady() prints exactly that sentence — code 'no-depot', fix 'Build a Freight Depot in your city' — to a player whose save already holds one. The discriminator is published and unused: the api exposes ready: () => !!makeHost() (public/src/city/index.js:106). Add an 'inert-city' branch on MP.ready() before the no-depot branch; also fix the two false claims (see evidence).
evidence: AC pass, run not assumed: `node --check` OK on both; auditCatalog() -> []; effect(1)={bays:2,fleetCap:4,radius:4}, effect(3)={bays:6,fleetCap:12,radius:6}; missingPrereqs('freightdepot',[])=['powerplant']; cityProdDef('depot').name still 'Supply Workshop'; git show --stat: production.data.js 132 +/- with zero deletions, cost.js untouched; node _synckcheck.mjs -> ALL CLEAN. Nine-state drive of depot.js (no window / window-no-bridge / bridge-no-city / city-no-placed / full with null+string+wrong-defId+level'99'+missing-level rows / placed() throws / effect() throws / null nodeId): never a throw, never undefined, level '99' clamped to 3, codes no-bridge, no-city, no-depot, unreadable, no-origin each carrying why+fix. FALSE CLAIM 1 (depot.js:~205, depots()): 'Handing back only the nested shape would mean inReach(bestDepot(), ...) and quote({depot:bestDepot()}) resolve to present: false, and routes.js would then refuse the haul with "no depot"'. Measured: routes.js resolveDepot() takes present from nodeId (flat in both shapes) and falls back to reach = 3 + level, so inReach({id,level:2,nodeId:'H1',effect:{...}},'H1','B',nodes) returns TRUE, identical to the flat row. Only `bays` would read 0. The flat mirror is still right, but the stated consequence is invented. FALSE CLAIM 2 (depot.js:~296, fleetCap()): 'index.js calls this as call(fleetCap, 0, b) - it passes the BRIDGE as the first argument - and Number(bridge) is NaN, so that path scores tier 0'. index.js:384 and :393 pass call(fleetCap, 0, 0), and index.js:357-364 explicitly records that change ('Passing 0 makes the intent explicit instead of leaving the correct behaviour resting on a coincidence'). The same comment also attributes `depot.fleetCap + garage.slotBonus` to depotBlock(); it is in buildView() at index.js:560. GAP: public/src/city/index.js:106 `ready: () => !!makeHost()` is never consulted by depot.js (grep: MP.ready() absent), so the inert-bridge case falls through to the no-depot sentence.
